title: Building Your First Mutual Fund Portfolio at 25: An Ideal Approach
description: Starting early with mutual funds at 25 provides a significant advantage due to the power of compounding. Focus on aligning your investments with specific fina.

faq.q: How much should a 25-year-old invest in mutual funds?
faq.a: The ideal amount depends on your income, expenses, and financial goals. A common thumb rule is to invest at least 20-30% of your net monthly income, but focus on what you can consistently afford without compromising your emergency fund.

faq.q: Should I invest directly or through a distributor?
faq.a: Direct plans have lower expense ratios as they don't involve distributor commissions, leading to higher returns over the long term. Regular plans go through distributors who can offer advice. For informed investors, direct plans are generally preferred.

faq.q: What is the difference between an ELSS fund and other equity funds?
faq.a: ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) funds are diversified equity mutual funds that offer tax benefits under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, 1961. They come with a mandatory lock-in period of three years, unlike other open-ended equity funds.

faq.q: How often should I review my mutual fund portfolio?
faq.a: It's advisable to review your portfolio at least once a year, or whenever there's a significant change in your financial situation, goals, or market conditions. This helps ensure your investments remain aligned with your objectives.

faq.q: Can NRIs invest in Indian mutual funds?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can invest in Indian mutual funds, though the process and permissible funds may vary based on their country of residence and specific regulations. They typically need an NRE or NRO bank account and a KYC-compliant status.

faq.q: What is a Consolidated Account Statement (CAS)?
faq.a: A CAS provides a single, unified view of all your mutual fund holdings across different fund houses, along with your demat account holdings. It's a crucial document for tracking your investments and can be requested from depositories.
